title: Perimeter and Area
seo_title: Grade 3 Perimeter and Area Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Perimeter: investigate the distance around 2-D shapes and 3-D objects using rulers or informal units. Area: investigate the area of shapes using tiling (counting squares).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: perimeter by adding sides, perimeter of rectangles, and area by counting squares. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Perimeter is the distance all the way around a shape.
  • Add all the sides: a rectangle has 2 long and 2 short sides.
  • Area is the space inside a shape: count the squares.
  • Perimeter is a length (cm); area is counted in squares.

Examples

Example

A rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm

5 + 3 + 5 + 3

Answer: 16 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Squares for perimeterCount the edges around the outside.
Two sides onlyAdd all 4 sides.
Perimeter or areaAround or inside?

items.q: A rectangle is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A rectangle has 4 sides. Opposite sides are the same length, so the sides are 6, 4, 6 and 4. 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. Adding only 6 + 4 = 10 leaves out two sides.

items.q: All the sides of this hexagon are the same length. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides. 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 24 m.

items.q: A square has sides of 6 m. What is its perimeter?
items.e: A square has 4 sides the same length: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 24 m. You can also use the 4 times table: 4 × 6 = 24.

items.q: The perimeter of this triangle is 18 cm. How long is the missing side?
items.e: Add the sides you know: 6 + 7 = 13. Then take that away from the perimeter: 18 − 13 = 5 cm. Check: 6 + 5 + 7 = 18.

items.q: The perimeter of this triangle is 27 cm. How long is the missing side?
items.e: Add the sides you know: 9 + 10 = 19. Then take that away from the perimeter: 27 − 19 = 8 cm. Check: 9 + 8 + 10 = 27.

items.q: The perimeter of this triangle is 29 cm. How long is the missing side?

items.q: The perimeter of this triangle is 33 m. How long is the missing side?

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 m. It is 9 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two long sides are 9 + 9 = 18 m. 24 − 18 = 6 m is left for the two short sides. Half of 6 is 3, so each short side is 3 m.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 m. It is 12 m long. How wide is it?
items.e: The two long sides are 12 + 12 = 24 m. 36 − 24 = 12 m is left for the two short sides. Half of 12 is 6, so each short side is 6 m.

items.q: The perimeter of this rectangle is 32 cm. How long is the missing side?
items.e: The two long sides are 11 + 11 = 22 cm. 32 − 22 = 10 cm is left for the two short sides. Half of 10 is 5, so each short side is 5 cm.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Count the shaded squares, row by row: 4 + 4 + 6 = 14. The area is 14 cm². Count each square once, not the sides around the edge (that would be the perimeter, 18).

items.q: What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: Count the squares inside, row by row: 3 rows of 4 is 4, 8, 12. The area is 12 square units. (14 is the number of sides around the edge: that is the perimeter.)

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Count the shaded squares, row by row: 6 + 6 + 6 + 3 = 21. The area is 21 cm². Count each square once, not the sides around the edge (that would be the perimeter, 22).

items.q: What is the area of the shaded shape?

items.q: What is the area of the shaded triangle? Two half squares make one whole square.
items.e: There are 6 whole squares and 4 half squares. 4 halves make 2 whole squares. 6 + 2 = 8 square units.

items.q: A shape on a grid covers 8 whole squares and 4 half squares. What is its area in square units?

items.q: Kyle has 50 cm of ribbon. He wants to put it round a square photo frame with sides of 12 cm. Does he have enough?
items.e: Perimeter: 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 = 48 cm. 50 − 48 = 2 cm, so there is enough with 2 cm left.

items.q: A square tablecloth has sides of 90 cm. Grandma sews lace round the edge. How much lace does she need?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 90 + 90 + 90 + 90 = 360 cm. (4 × 9 = 36, so 4 × 90 = 360.)

items.q: A square garden has sides of 8 m. Fence panels are 2 m long. How many panels go all the way round?
items.e: Perimeter: 8 + 8 + 8 + 8 = 32 m. Each panel is 2 m: 32 ÷ 2 = 16 panels.

items.q: A rabbit run is 6 m long and 4 m wide. One long side is against a wall, so it needs no fence. How much fence is needed for the other sides?
items.e: Only 3 sides need fence: 6 + 4 + 4 = 14 m.

items.q: A flower bed is a triangle. Its sides are 4 m, 5 m and 6 m. Mr Patel puts edging all the way round. How much edging does he use?
items.e: Add the 3 sides: 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 m.

items.q: Zanele walks round a path shaped like a triangle. Its sides are 30 m, 40 m and 50 m. Sibusiso walks round a square path with sides of 35 m. Who walks further?
items.e: Zanele: 30 + 40 + 50 = 120 m. Sibusiso: 35 + 35 + 35 + 35 = 140 m. 140 − 120 = 20 m, so Sibusiso walks 20 m further.

items.q: Zinhle sticks ribbon round the edge of a birthday card. The card is 15 cm long and 10 cm wide. How much ribbon does she need?
items.e: Ribbon goes all the way round: 15 + 10 + 15 + 10 = 50 cm. The card is measured in cm, so the answer is in cm.

items.q: The school playground is a rectangle 40 m long and 25 m wide. Ruan walks once round the edge. How far does he walk?
items.e: Once round is the perimeter: 40 + 25 + 40 + 25 = 130 m.

items.q: A square sandpit has a perimeter of 12 m. How long is each side?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 m. Check: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12 m.

items.q: Ofentse puts a paper border round a display board. The board is 150 cm long and 100 cm wide. How long is the border?
items.e: Border round the edge: 150 + 100 + 150 + 100 = 500 cm.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded tree shape?
items.e: There are 6 whole squares and 4 half squares. 4 halves make 2 whole squares. 6 + 2 = 8 cm².

items.q: Which unit is best for measuring the length of the school hallway?
items.e: This is a length, not an area. A hallway is long, so use metres. cm and m are for lengths; cm² and m² are for areas.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded arrow shape?
items.e: There are 8 whole squares and 4 half squares. 4 halves make 2 whole squares. 8 + 2 = 10 cm².

items.q: Which is bigger: 5 m² or 50 cm²?
items.e: 1 m² is a square 1 m (100 cm) on each side. Even one m² is far bigger than 50 squares of 1 cm². Look at the unit, not only the number.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Count the squares, row by row: 4 + 4 + 4 + 2 = 14. Each square is 1 cm², so the area is 14 cm². Area uses square units: cm², not cm.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Count the squares, row by row: 5 + 3 + 2 = 10. Each square is 1 cm², so the area is 10 cm². Area uses square units: cm², not cm.

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded sailboat shape?

items.q: This is a plan of a classroom reading corner. Each square is 1 m². What is its area?

items.q: Each square is 1 cm². What is the area of the shaded shape?
items.e: Count the squares, row by row: 1 + 1 + 5 = 7. Each square is 1 cm², so the area is 7 cm². Area uses square units: cm², not cm.

items.q: This is a plan of a school garden. Each square is 1 m². What is its area?
items.e: Count the squares: 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 = 12. Each square is 1 m², so the area is 12 m².
